feed.description: Software engineering conversations: reliability, architecture, delivery, and the tradeoffs nobody puts in the blog post.
feed.title: Practical Systems

bullets: Alert fatigue is a signal-to-noise problem rather than a discipline problem — when a team ignores pages, the pages are wrong, not the people.
Tuning the alerts should come before tuning the humans; fixing the paging system addresses the root cause, whereas pushing responders to try harder does not.
The share of pages that led to action is the key diagnostic metric — under half signals a noise problem.
Noise cannot be overcome through willpower; no amount of responder effort compensates for alerts that don't warrant action, so the fix has to live in the alerting itself.
